description: Bufferbloat (docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md #14). Three phases (idle, download, upload); each lists the ping samples per target in measuring order (null = lost; the first 2 s of a loaded phase already dropped), the load reached in Mbps (null while idle) and the load error, if any. Optional per loaded phase: capped (the load stopped at its byte limit, so the line may be faster), refused (HTTP status when the test server refused the load) and retry_after_s (the wait it asked for). A direction that was not measured or not fully loaded cannot make the result ok.

cases.name: healthy line: no advice
boundary: +29 ms is ok
boundary: +30 ms is a warning
boundary: +100 ms is still a warning
boundary: +101 ms is bad
the worse direction decides
only the Internet rises: queue on the WAN hop
the router rises too: queue on the local hop
30% of pings lost under load is bad even if survivors are fast
boundary: 20% lost with unchanged latency is bad and explained as loss
boundary: 17.5% lost is still ok
all pings lost under load: rise without bound
no idle replies from the Internet
a load under 1 Mbps did not load the line
one direction could not load, the other is judged
no router target
3 samples per phase: even the idle phase is too short
boundary: 7 samples under load are ignored, 8 are judged
fewer than 8 samples in both loaded phases: no result
p95 and median from uneven samples (odd count)
p95 from fewer than 20 samples is the maximum; even-count median
lossy while idle but fine under load
upload phase failed entirely and download is clean
download refused by the test server: no ok from the upload alone
refused without Retry-After: try again later
both directions refused: no result, wait for the server
a load stopped at its byte limit cannot vouch for ok
a rise seen at the byte limit is still reported
